items.title: Luke Schiro Interview, 1967-12-05
items.q: They played the footage right when Tony's Ron came in.

ctx.x: I remember when he died. And then we played at the old, let's see, the Roma Cafe, which was on Decatur Street. It was across the street from the Morning Call. It was the coffee shop there. Uh huh. See, it's a restaurant. It was upstairs, over the restaurant. There's a Roma restaurant there, yeah. Yeah, well, yeah. Well, that's the same spot upstairs. There was a beer joint there. Uh huh. And we had Arthur Sealy going banjo at the time. Uh huh. And, let's see, Joe Stevens on drums. That's the, look, Rag Baby…
Yeah, I heard him with Fuji Rack. Yeah. They played the footage right when Tony's Ron came in.

Yeah. And then, uh, we see, up there, Clara, and that's there, and sox. Uh huh. And then from there we went to the Wonder Bar on Decatur Street. They was at the Queer Joint. And, uh, we had, uh, let's see, Joe Stevenson's gang there. And Brett Dimmons on piano. And we had, uh, Tweety on trumpet, myself. And, uh, you know, they thought the band was, uh, they thought the band was, uh, queer so we quit. Uh huh. Well, and those places had been kept by the square. Yeah. And then there was another spot on Decatur…
